content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has developed the National Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP), which is designed to provide structured lifestyle modification programs aimed at delaying or preventing the onset of type 2 diabetes. Programs such as the Medicare Diabetes Prevention Program (MDPP) offer behavioral counseling services specifically tailored for individuals who are overweight and at a high risk of developing diabetes. Eligibility for coverage under the MDPP requires a body mass index (BMI) of at least 25 kg/m², or 23 kg/m² for Asian Americans, ensuring that individuals at significant risk receive the necessary interventions. However, access to these programs can be limited for some individuals due to barriers such as geographic location and financial constraints. Efforts to expand coverage through Medicare and Medicaid, as well as the inclusion of registered dietitian nutritionists (RDNs) and community health workers in these programs, have been shown to enhance both the accessibility and the overall effectiveness of diabetes prevention initiatives.
